plan: This is structurally a second-price auction: my sealed bid acts as my exit point in the ascending clock, and if I win, I pay the second-highest bid (the price where the last competitor exits), not my own bid. Bidding my true value ($30) is the dominant strategy—bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me, while bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. I'll bid exactly my value to maximize expected profit.

Since this functions as a second-price auction—the winner pays the second-highest bid (the price at which the second-to-last bidder exits)—the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids (profitable) and lose when it doesn't (avoiding losses), while paying only the second-highest bid if I win. There's no incentive to shade or inflate my bid.

Since this functions as a second-price auction (the clock ends when the second-highest bidder exits, and the winner pays that price), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding higher risks overpaying above my value, while bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With a value of $6, bidding exactly $6 ensures I only win when profitable and pay a fair price determined by the second-highest bid.
